newsitem.title: POLAND: Daewoo ups Polish investment target.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo ups Polish investment target.

text.p: Daewoo Group plans to top its earlier investment pledges in Poland and see its total investment in the country reaching $1.5 billion by 2001, the head of the group's automotive division said on Monday.
"By the year 2001 we will increase our investments in Poland...we expect it roughly at $1.5 billion," Tae Gou Kim, the Chairman of Daewoo Motor Co. Ltd told a news conference.
He also said the company intended to increase its forecast of car production in Poland by 50 percent from earlier announced 200,000 by year 2000.
Earlier the company has set a $1.1 billion investment target.

Gou Kim, who came to Warsaw to reaffirm the company's commitment to Poland after the arrest of the head of Daewoo-FSO Motor Sok Chin-chol in Seoul, said the arrest would not affect Daewoo's activities here.

"We want to stress that Daewoo activities globally and in Poland are and will remain unaffected by the these developments ... we are not looking for a replacement and we believe in his innocence," he said.
On Saturday Sok Chin-chol, who was the president of Daewoo Heavy Industries last year and now heads the group's car subsidiary in Poland was arrested in Seoul in connection with an arms scandal.
Gou Kim said so far Daewoo Group has invested $74 million in Poland and expected to double this by the end of this year.

The group, which besides the Warsaw car factory comprises a van factory in Lublin, eastern Poland, and a consumer electronics subsidiary near Warsaw, expects its sales in Poland to reach $1.2 billion this year and $1.9 billion in 1997.
